result.title: A Bifurcation-Theoretic Framework for the Controllability of Emergent Intelligent Systems
result.summary: Real-world intelligent systems must reconcile two demands: the adaptability conferred by emergence and the steerability required for accountable deployment. We show that these demands are governed by two distinct bifurcations on the same object and that, consequently, increased capability does not imply increased controllability. Emergence is a bifurcation of the capability variable $S$, with criterion $Γ:=\mathcal F'(0)>1$ equivalent to the existence of a unique positive stable fixed point of a self-consistency equation, following solely from the concavity of $\mathcal F$. Controllability is a bifurcation of the permission variable $c$, whose dynamics include an erosion term and exhibit a saddle-node fold with hysteresis as the gate criterion $ρ^\ast$ crosses unity. Three quantitative results follow: the critical exponent distinguishes families rather than classifying the transition; the gating-cost bound $K(M)\propto\log(1+M)$ grows with scope, not capability; and the fold threshold is $γ_c\approx4μκ$. Calibrated in both directions, the criteria reproduce the two-dimensional Ising transition, admit two true-feedback order parameters, and reject nine candidate quantities, supporting the conclusion that the order parameter is geometric rather than capability-related. Since permission cannot be endogenized and no deployed system has been measured to satisfy $Γ>1$ and $ρ^\ast>1$ simultaneously, increased capability does not imply controllability.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在同一动力学对象上区分两种分岔：涌现对应能力变量 S 的分岔（判据 Γ>1），可控性对应许可变量 c 的分岔（存在带滞回的鞍结折叠，阈值 γ_c≈4μκ），并推出临界指数只区分家族、门控成本按 K(M)∝log(1+M) 随范围增长等结论，主张能力提升不等于可控性提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「许可变量＋折叠滞回」的门控表述可能与 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的停止与计算门控决策、以及 latent 状态可操控性判断形成概念对应，可供核查；但该框架高度抽象且无多模态实验，能否操作化到 VLM 推理仍是推测。
